case_1_ambiguity_real_and_measurable.evidence: role_stability.json: 3/7 documents show the evidence vector strictly more stable than the observed role across repeated arms of the SAME document (table_shape_score constant at 4 across 19 arms each for cmb_stamp_table_vi and hc_stamp_table_vi, while the observed role flips); 0/7 show the reverse.

case_2_evidence_too_weak_currently.evidence: adversarial_controls.json: 6/20 synthetic misfires against the current scoring rule, including a SEVERE one -- ordinary single-column prose (justified paragraphs, bullet lists) can reach the conservative threshold using ONLY row-based criteria, with zero column evidence required, because table_shape_score accumulates points from 5 independently-scored criteria rather than requiring row AND column evidence jointly.

case_3_hard_label_not_true_bottleneck.evidence: role_contract.json Phase 2: the label-collapsing pattern recurs beyond table/picture -- 18/28 detector-label keys map INCONSISTENTLY between the scanned-page route and the whole-document route (checkbox_selected/unselected, 57 real historical instances, silently becomes ElementType.OTHER on the route this repository actually exercises, despite being correctly wired for the unused route). The table/picture question 031 and 032 both centered on is ONE instance of a broader label-consistency problem, not the sole bottleneck.

case_4_helps_table_recovery_hurts_genera.evidence: routing_policy_results.json: the tested dual-candidate policy (2/3) shows ZERO change to Layer-1 text/char recall on the negative and 'other' document populations, in either direction (031 intervention_results.json, reused here) -- no evidence of general-semantics harm was found. This does not mean no harm exists (adversarial_controls.json's prose misfire was never tested against real running text in the historical corpus), but the CASE-4 specific claim (helps tables, hurts general semantics) has no supporting evidence found this milestone.

phase_19_research_frontier.conclusion: Case 1 AND Case 2 are BOTH supported simultaneously -- this is not a contradiction: ambiguity is real and measurable (Case 1) AND the current evidence model is not yet reliable enough to act on unconditionally (Case 2). Case 3 adds that the SCOPE of the underlying problem (label collapsing/inconsistency) is broader than table-label gating alone.
